report.summary: Chunk 6 of drift.py: builds state dict, ScanResult, and defines Acceptance dataclass. Verifies claims about classification handling, dark switch filtering, unparsable aggregation, and state counts.
risks: dark_switches filtering | medium | Filters out switches where docs.documents(sw.name) exists, but doc_drift entries are still added even if documented. Could cause inconsistency if a switch appears in both dark and doc_drift. | Check if a switch can simultaneously satisfy both conditions; if so, clarify intent or add exclusion.

unparsable set | low | Both reach_report.unparsable and switch_report.unparsable are added to the same set, but switch_report.unparsable items are strings (split on ':') while reach_report.unparsable are module names. Could be mismatched types. | Verify the actual types of items in these collections.

sites dictionary keys | low | Keys like 'island:module' are used, but there is no check for duplicate keys (e.g., same module name appearing in multiple categories). Later entries overwrite earlier ones silently. | Confirm whether a module can belong to multiple categories; if so, decide on priority or use list values.

handoff.purpose: Build state dictionary, sites mapping, and define Acceptance dataclass for drift analysis.

symbols.name: Acceptance
symbols.note: Dataclass representing an acceptance item with fields: item, why, since, until, who, problem. Has a property 'valid' that returns True if problem is empty.

claims.text: TEST ONLY is a property of an UNREACHED module, not of an island specifically. Scoping it to islands meant a shim or an unknown whose only importer was a test could not be described that way at all.
claims.why: The code defines unreached_facts as all facts with classification in UNREACHED_CLASSES (which includes islands, unknown, shims), then test_only filters those where m.tested_by is truthy. This matches the claim: test-only is derived from unreached modules, not just islands.

claims.text: Two engines disagreeing about the import graph. reach REPORTS these and refuses to merge them (see reach.analyse); the gate is where a disagreement that persists across a commit becomes somebody's problem.
claims.why: The code assigns index_extra_edges from reach_report.index_extra_edges, but the behavior of reach.analyse regarding refusal to merge is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: An absent API key is not a dark feature. The feature it belongs to is documented and merely unconfigured -- ``daedalus doctor`` already reports it, and an architecture gate is a poor place to enumerate which secrets a machine is missing. ``secret`` is the switch engine's own classification, so this is a filter over one answer, not a second opinion about what a switch is.
claims.why: The code explicitly checks `if sw.kind == "secret": continue`, filtering out secret switches from dark features, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: A module the scanner could not parse contributes nothing to either engine's answer, which makes it a hole in the map that used to be filled by a bare ``continue``. It is a finding, not a shrug.
claims.why: The code creates a set unparsable from reach_report.unparsable and adds entries from switch_report.unparsable (after splitting on ':' and stripping), treating them as findings included in the state.

claims.text: The honest total: every module on disk that no entry point reaches, whatever reach called it. It is the number the page has to add up to, and it is what "islands=7" used to hide.
claims.why: The code computes 'unreached' as len(islands) + len(unknown_mods) + len(shims), summing all unreached classifications, consistent with the claim that it's the total of unreached modules regardless of subcategory.

claims.text: An absent API key is not a dark feature.
claims.why: Code filters out switches with kind == 'secret' before adding to dark dict, so secret switches (API keys) are excluded.

observations.what: The code filters out dark switches if they are documented (docs.documents(sw.name) is truthy). However, doc_drift entries are added for all switches in switch_report.drift, regardless of documentation status. A switch could appear in both dark and doc_drift if it is dark but documented? Actually the dark filter skips documented switches, so a documented switch would not be in dark. But a switch could be undocumented and dark, and also have drift? Possibly.

The unparsable set aggregates items from reach_report.unparsable (likely module names) and switch_report.unparsable (strings like 'module:error'). The code splits the latter on ':' and takes the first part. This assumes the format is always 'module:...' without colons in the module name.

The 'sites' dictionary is built with string keys like 'island:' + m. If the same module name appears in multiple categories, later entries overwrite earlier ones. No deduplication or priority is applied.
The Acceptance dataclass has a 'valid' property that returns True if problem is empty. It does not validate other fields like dates or who.
